title: HE STARTED STRONG.
paragraphs: HE STARTED STRONG.

One step out of the boat.
Wind screaming.
Waves clawing at his knees.

And for a moment—
he was doing the impossible.

Open loop? Here it is:
How do you go from walking on water…
to choking on it?
Let’s talk about Gospel of Matthew 14:22–33.
The storm wasn’t gentle. It was violent. The Sea of Galilee can turn from glass to chaos in minutes. The disciples were seasoned fishermen—and still afraid.
Then they saw Him.
A figure on the water.
They thought it was a ghost.
But it was Jesus.
And Peter—oh Peter—did what most of us post about but rarely practice.
He said, “Lord, if it’s You, command me to come.”
That’s bold faith.
And Jesus answered with one word:
“Come.”

No life jacket.
No safety net.
Just a voice.
Peter swung his legs over the boat. Wet wood under his toes. Wind tearing at his robe. Heart pounding against his ribs.
And he walked.
On water.
Don’t miss that. Before he sank, he walked. He experienced supernatural obedience.
But here’s the turn.
“When he saw the wind, he was afraid…”
He shifted his focus.

Eyes off Christ.
Eyes on chaos.
And immediately—he began to sink.

Not when he stepped out.
Not when the storm hit.
When he looked away.
That’s us.

We start strong.
New year devotion streak.
Bold prayer.
Clean break from that secret sin.
Then the wind picks up. Bills stack. Temptation whispers. Old habits knock.
And fear floods the lungs.
But here’s the Gospel pivot.
Peter didn’t drown in silence.
He cried, “Lord, save me!”
Three words.

No theology degree.
No polished prayer.
Just desperation.
And the text says immediately Jesus reached out His hand.
Immediately.

Not after a lecture.
Not after shame.
Immediately.

Some scholars interpret this moment as a rebuke of “little faith.” Others see it as training—Jesus stretching Peter’s trust beyond the boat. But both agree on this: Peter was saved by Jesus’ grip, not by his balance.
Hear me.

You are not sustained by how strong you start.
You are sustained by Who holds you when you falter.

Peter sank because he feared.
We sink because of sin.
And sin is deeper than water. It separates us from a holy God. No human effort can walk across that gap.
That’s why Jesus didn’t just stretch out His hand on the sea.
He stretched out His hands on a cross.

At Gospel of Matthew 14, He saves a drowning disciple.
At Calvary, He saves a drowning world.

The storm didn’t disqualify Peter.
The sinking didn’t cancel his calling.
This same Peter would preach at Pentecost. This same Peter would write letters soaked in hope. Failure was not his final chapter—Jesus was.
So if you started strong… and now you’re sinking—
Cry out.

Not eloquently.
Honestly.
“Lord, save me.”
And watch the hand of Christ cut through the wind.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
